passages.text: There’s no privacy in the world, for someone who does bad deeds. You’ll know for yourself, whether you’ve lied or told the truth.
This life, so very short, is led onward. One led on to old age has no shelter. Seeing this peril in death, do good deeds that bring you joy.
passages.note: life's shortness and doing good while you can

passages.text: When your house is on fire, you rescue the pot that’s useful, not the one that’s burnt. And as the world is on fire with old age and death, you should rescue by giving, for what’s given is rescued.
passages.note: mortality and the lasting value of generosity

passages.text: A hateful person, overcome by hate, intends to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They experience mental pain and sadness. When hate has been given up, they don’t intend to hurt themselves, hurt others, and hurt both. They don’t experience mental pain and sadness.
passages.note: how hatred causes suffering and letting it go
